hero.h1: Resources for Titanium Dioxide Procurement Decisions
hero.body: Explore technical guides, sourcing research and market updates created to support titanium dioxide procurement decisions across grades, applications and destination markets.

evidencePrinciples.heading: How We Use Evidence
evidencePrinciples.intro: Use these principles when applying research to a procurement decision.

items.heading: Technical comparisons
items.body: Comparisons describe defined technical criteria and should not be interpreted as automatic product equivalence.

items.heading: Application relevance
items.body: Grade suitability depends on application and processing requirements and should be checked against the relevant technical documentation.

items.heading: Current trade information
items.body: Time-sensitive trade information should identify its official source, applicable scope, source date and review date.

buyerQuestions.question: What should buyers compare when evaluating titanium dioxide grades?
buyerQuestions.answer: Buyers should compare the intended application, processing requirements, grade-specific technical data and relevant technical documentation. Performance values should be compared using compatible test methods and current documents. Final suitability should be validated in the buyer’s formulation or processing system.

buyerQuestions.question: Does a technical comparison mean two titanium dioxide grades are equivalent?
buyerQuestions.answer: No. A technical comparison can organize criteria such as documented properties, application requirements and process considerations, but it does not prove identical performance or interchangeability. Equivalence requires evidence for the specific grades and the buyer’s use conditions.

buyerQuestions.question: How should application requirements affect titanium dioxide grade selection?
buyerQuestions.answer: Application and processing requirements determine which technical criteria need to be checked. Coatings, plastics, masterbatch, printing inks and paper can place different demands on a titanium dioxide grade, so buyers should use the relevant technical documentation and application-specific validation rather than a generic recommendation.

buyerQuestions.question: Why does the date of trade information matter?
buyerQuestions.answer: Trade measures, investigations and regulatory requirements can change over time and may apply only to a defined product, origin, period or procedure. Procurement teams should check the current official source, applicable scope, source date and review date before relying on titanium dioxide trade information.

buyerQuestions.question: Where can buyers find current titanium dioxide market information for the EU, UK, India or Brazil?
buyerQuestions.answer: Use the relevant TiO2 Malaysia market page for destination-specific procurement context. Detailed trade information should be used only when a dedicated update identifies its official source, scope and dates; the Resources Hub does not infer a current policy outcome.

resourceRelations.title: EU Titanium Dioxide Anti-Dumping Duty: Current Measure and 2026 Review
resourceRelations.summary: Check the current EU anti-dumping measure for specified China-origin titanium dioxide, the 2026 reinvestigation and shipment inputs to verify.
resourceRelations.ctaLabel: EU Titanium Dioxide Anti-Dumping Duty: Current Measure and 2026 Review
resourceRelations.applicableScope: the titanium dioxide product defined in the regulation when it originates in the People's Republic of China
resourceRelations.publicStatusLabel: As checked on 7 September 2026, EUR-Lex marks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/4 as in force. It sets fixed anti-dumping duties for the titanium dioxide product defined in the regulation when it originates in the People's Republic of China. A notice published on 25 August 2026 reopened an absorption reinvestigation, but that notice did not replace the current fixed-duty table.

resourceRelations.ctaLabel: UK Rutile Titanium Dioxide: Active AD0086 Investigation and Import Registration
resourceRelations.applicableScope: specified rutile titanium dioxide goods originating in China
resourceRelations.publicStatusLabel: As checked on 7 September 2026, the UK Trade Remedies Authority lists AD0086 as an active dumping investigation into specified rutile titanium dioxide goods originating in China. HMRC has also been directed to register the specified imports from 27 March 2026.

resourceRelations.title: India Titanium Dioxide Anti-Dumping Duty: 2025 Levy Quashed, 2026 Recommendation Explained
resourceRelations.summary: Check the quashed 2025 India TiO2 levy, DGTR’s 2026 recommendation, product scope, producer paths and shipment inputs to verify.
resourceRelations.ctaLabel: India Titanium Dioxide Anti-Dumping Duty: 2025 Levy Quashed, 2026 Recommendation Explained
resourceRelations.officialSourceName: DGTR remand final findings dated 3 August 2026
resourceRelations.applicableScope: specified origin, export and producer paths
resourceRelations.publicStatusLabel: As checked on 7 September 2026, the 2025 titanium dioxide anti-dumping final findings and implementing levy were quashed. DGTR issued fresh remand final findings on 3 August 2026 and recommended anti-dumping amounts for specified origin, export and producer paths.

resourceRelations.title: Brazil Titanium Dioxide Anti-Dumping Duty: Current Measure, Scope and Rates
resourceRelations.summary: Check Brazil’s definitive TiO2 anti-dumping measure, China-origin scope, four USD/t bands, exclusions and shipment inputs to verify.
resourceRelations.ctaLabel: Brazil Titanium Dioxide Anti-Dumping Duty: Current Measure, Scope and Rates
resourceRelations.officialSourceName: Resolution GECEX 802/2025 in the Diário Oficial da União
resourceRelations.applicableScope: the specified rutile titanium dioxide product originating in China
resourceRelations.publicStatusLabel: As checked on 7 September 2026, Brazil’s MDIC measures-in-force index lists a definitive anti-dumping duty on the specified rutile titanium dioxide product originating in China. Resolution GECEX 802/2025 sets four producer/exporter bands, and the official index lists the measure through 24 October 2030, subject to later official decisions.
